stem: In the figure, points \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) lie on the circle with center \(O\). The measure of angle \(ACB\) is \(55^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(AOB\)?
solution: Angle \(ACB\) is an inscribed angle and angle \(AOB\) is the central angle that intercepts the same arc \(AB\).
A central angle is twice the inscribed angle on the same arc: \(2 \cdot 55 = 110\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This halves the inscribed angle; the central angle is twice it, not half.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The central angle is not equal to the inscribed angle; it is twice as large.
explanation.C: Correct. The central angle \(AOB\) is twice the inscribed angle \(ACB\): \(2(55) = 110\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(180 - 55 = 125\) treats the two angles as supplementary, which they are not.

verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert all(abs(d('O',q)-6)<0.01 for q in 'ABC') and abs(ang('A','C','B')-55)<0.1
ans=2*55
assert abs(ang('A','O','B')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==110
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
